doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Closing: Utica, Rochester and Major Holly
summary: Thanks and talk of upstate New York clubs and playing with Major Holly.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: You did, a real long way. And I’ve really enjoyed talking with you today, and I wish you the best and I hope that we are in town sometimes when you’re playing somewhere.
I hope so, I hope so. I guess I’ll never be up your way.
Yup. Right outside Utica. Not a lot of clubs there either, unfortunately.
I’m trying to think the last time I worked — I never worked in Utica — but Rochester.
Rochester and Syracuse you might have been. I think I told you I saw you in Syracuse with Major Holly.
Right. Yeah I worked with Major up there and some other place too right off the Thruway, I forgot the name of it. Rochester, yeah, there used to be a club called Back Stage. Is that true?
I think so and there was the Pythod Room.
There, yeah, the Pythod, I remember that, the Pythod, long ago.
Right. Well thanks for your time today. I’m most appreciative.
A pleasure indeed, I enjoyed it.
